claims_about_writeup.quote: contribution.md has the method, mechanism, and the negative results
claims_about_writeup.why: The write-up does contain a 'What the method is' section describing the method, a 'Why it works, and where the idea came from' section covering mechanism, and a 'What I found along the way' section documenting the swept negative results (~15 ruled-out directions).
contribution.md does contain the fuller account of the method, mechanism, and negative-result sweep summarized in the message.

message_source_quote: Raman's contrast is *think vs don't-think* — Wegner's active suppression, where the forbidden concept paradoxically stays active, so the contrast partially cancels the signal it wants. Mine is *retention vs passive release*
writeup_source_quote: Raman et al.'s white-bear result shows the association failure is a *representation* problem, not a lens problem
rationale: Both documents name Raman's white-bear work explicitly, explain that its think-vs-don't-think contrast partially cancels the suppression signal it is trying to isolate, and claim the new retain-vs-release direction is a distinct, cleaner stance direction that scores higher (0.775 vs ≈0.69) on the same setup. Neither document overstates or understates this relationship relative to the other — the crediting, the overlap framing, and the novelty claim are stated in essentially identical terms in both places.
